items.basis: The candidate claims the 120-micron second stage removes aggregate nuclei above 120 microns, but flat-fan spray nozzles in hot-rolling mills typically have internal passages and orifices smaller than 120 microns; particles passing the 120-micron wedge wire will still clog the nozzles, leaving the mechanism physically incomplete for its stated purpose. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "a two-stage inertial wedge-wire cascade (300 then 120 micron) on the header supply removes scale particles and aggregate nuclei above 120 microns"

The candidate claims automatic backflush restores full flow without mill stop, but reverse-flow backflushing a supply header feeding 120 active spray nozzles requires isolating the header from the nozzles to prevent contaminated flush water from being forced backward through the nozzle orifices into the roll bite; this isolation interrupts cooling, constituting a mill stop or a direct violation of the continuous operation boundary during rolling. GROUNDED_IN: RECORD "restores full flow without mill stop" | SCOPE "no mill stop for installation or operation"
